dl.next: Windows installer, macOS app, Raspberry Pi/Linux .deb: the till opens in its own app window — no browser, no terminal. Windows: run the installer, then launch "Universal Till" from the Start menu/desktop shortcut. macOS: open the .dmg, drag Universal Till into Applications and open it — the app is Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple, so macOS only asks you once to confirm. Raspberry Pi/Debian/Ubuntu .deb: after sudo apt install ./unitill-pos_*.deb, "Universal Till" is in your applications menu. Portable .tar.gz/.zip archives: on Windows and Linux, double-click unitill-desktop.exe / unitill-desktop for the same app-window experience; run-unitill.command/.sh/.bat opens your default browser instead. The macOS portable archive is not notarized: the first time, macOS blocks run-unitill.command — open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway. Dedicated Raspberry Pi till (no desktop needed): on a fresh Raspberry Pi OS Lite install, reboot once after installing the .deb — the first boot sets up the kiosk, and from then on the Pi starts straight into the till, fullscreen, no desktop at all. On Raspberry Pi OS with Desktop, the till opens fullscreen on top of the desktop when you log in; Settings → Display → "Exit to OS window" (manager PIN) takes you back to the desktop.

faq.a1: Yes. EPOS (electronic point of sale), POS, till system and cash register all mean the software you ring up sales on. Universal Till gives you a touch sale screen, barcode scanning, receipts, stock and sales reports.
faq.a2: Yes. The till itself is free forever on your own hardware: open source under the MIT licence, no monthly fee for the core. Paid plans have no minimum term on monthly billing; in Germany, the managed TSE line (optional, from Shop) has a 12-month minimum per activated main till. Optional cloud extras, such as off-site backup, may cost extra, and card payments carry your card provider's own fees.
faq.a3: Yes. A full sale completes with no internet at all, and everything works locally on the till. Syncing is a bonus, never a requirement. A card reader still needs whatever connection its own provider requires.
faq.a4: A Raspberry Pi, an old PC or laptop, a mini-PC or a proper touch terminal — there are downloads for Windows, macOS, Linux, Raspberry Pi and Android. The iPhone and iPad apps are in internal testing (not on the App Store yet). A complete DIY till costs from about £70.
faq.a5: Yes. We never sit in your money flow: use any card machine and any processor — no fee creep, no frozen payouts.
faq.a6: Yes. Export your catalogue from your current system and import it: Loyverse, Square, SumUp and Shopify exports are recognised automatically, and any CSV or Excel file with name and price columns works. You see a preview before anything is saved.
